narrationScript: Now it's time to get hands-on and apply what we've learned! Your task is to build a simple Python script that manages a to-do list, with all tasks stored in an SQLite database. This exercise will help you solidify your understanding of how applications connect to databases and perform fundamental operations. You'll start by setting up the database connection and creating the `tasks` table if it doesn't already exist. Then, you'll implement the core CRUD operations. First, `add_task` will allow users to create new to-do items, specifying a description and an optional due date. Remember to use parameterized queries here for security! Next, `list_tasks` will retrieve and display all current tasks, showing their ID, description, due date, and status. Then, `update_task_status` will enable changing a task's status, for example, from 'pending' to 'completed'. And finally, `delete_task` will remove a task from the list based on its ID. As you work through these functions, pay close attention to how you establish and close your database connections, and how you execute your SQL commands. This activity is a practical application of all the connection and basic data manipulation concepts we've covered.
